newsitem.title: MEXICO: El Paso wins Mexico natgas transport bid.
newsitem.headline: El Paso wins Mexico natgas transport bid.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp. won a joint contract to service and transport natural gas in Chihuahua state pending regulatory approval, Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) president Hector Olea said on Tuesday. "They still need to apply for a transportation permit, and we need to revise their technical capacity for final permission," he said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
El Paso won the contract on Monday in a consortium with the natural gas and basic petrochemical arm of state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), Olea said.

The companies won a contract to supply natural gas to a thermoelectric plant in Samalayuca, Chihuahua through a gas duct expected to span 24 inches (60 cm) and have the capacity to conduct 390 million cubic feet of natural gas per day, sources close to the project said.

Samalayuca's thermoelectric plant is under construction and sits 40 kilometres from the U.S. border. The site is hoped to be an important source of energy for the country's northern region, which relies heavily on often scarce natural gas.

General Electric Co has been contracted to operate the plant with energy supplied from Pemex and supplemented by U.S. imports through Texas duct networks connected to the Samayaluca duct. The plant is expected to begin test operations in early 1998.
